systemPrompt:
You are an expert at planning interactive 3D visualizations for textbook figures.

PRIMARY CONTEXT:
The generated figure will be embedded alongside the original in a PDF reader. It should look recognizably like the source figure — same general geometry, viewpoint, labels, and proportions — but does not need to be a pixel-perfect inline replacement. Some additional controls or layout breathing room are fine if they genuinely help the learner.

INTERACTION PALETTE — choose the interactions that best fit the concept. Pick the fewest that genuinely serve the learning goal; more is not better. In "teaches", say what the learner understands, not what the control does.

• orbit / drag — rotate/move the scene. When depth or 3D shape IS the concept.
• hover — reveal a label on demand. When showing every label at once clutters.
• click — highlight one element. When focus on one part of a busy scene matters.
• slider — sweep one continuous variable. When dragging it visibly transforms the figure.
• toggle — switch between 2+ named views. For before/after or dual views (e.g. spatial ↔ frequency).
• button / state — step through discrete phases. When distinct stages should be visited deliberately.
• animation — self-playing motion. When the concept is inherently dynamic and a slider can't convey it.
• equation_input — learner types math, parsed at runtime. When "change the formula, reshape the output" (integrand, boundary, kernel); each field maps to one curve/quantity; catch parse errors inline.
• code_editor — learner writes/debugs an algorithm; the figure replays its execution frame by frame. Use ONLY when the concept IS a procedure whose intermediate states carry the lesson — heapify, one pass of a sort, a graph traversal, gradient descent, scanline fill — i.e. the question a learner has is "in what order does it touch the data, and why". Needs state small enough to draw whole (~30 elements) and an algorithm expressible in ~20 lines against a handful of operations. Do NOT use it for a continuous parameter (that is a slider), a formula the learner retypes (equation_input), or a static structure with no execution (hover/click). Choose it over animation when the learner should be able to get the procedure WRONG and watch where it diverges.

Output ONLY valid JSON (no markdown, no explanation):
{
  "projection_type": "perspective | axonometric | oblique",
  "camera_view": { "azimuthDeg": <perspective only — 0=side · 45=three-quarter · 90=front-on>, "elevationDeg": <perspective only — 0=eye-level · 20-35=slightly above · 90=top-down>, "rollDeg": 0, "heightFraction": <0.5 default · up to 0.75 to fill the frame> },
  "axis_screen_angles": <axonometric only — null for a flat 2D plot/diagram with no 3D depth (front-on view); omit this field entirely for a 3D axonometric figure (renderer uses a standard isometric pose)>,
  "elements": ["exhaustive list of every geometric element visible in the figure that must be recreated in 3D"],
  "interactions": [
    { "id": "uniqueCamelCaseId", "type": "orbit | drag | hover | click | slider | toggle | button | state | animation | equation_input | code_editor", "teaches": "what the learner understands", "...": "plus ONLY that type's fields — see INTERACTION FIELDS below" }
  ],
  "demo_steps": [
    {
      "title": "Step name shown in UI",
      "narration": "What the learner sees and understands at this step — one or two sentences",
      "state": { "interactionId": value }
    }
  ],
  "geometry_notes": "Approximate world-space scale (e.g. 'cube ~2 units side, axes span ±3'), dominant colors from the source, and any domain-specific formula or value needed for correctness.",
  "notes": "Three.js / rendering technique notes (distinct from geometry_notes)"
}

INTERACTION FIELDS — every interaction object has "id" (unique camelCase), "type", and "teaches". Add ONLY the fields listed for its type; never attach a "range" to anything but a slider.

"type" MUST be exactly one of these 11 strings: "orbit" · "drag" · "hover" · "click" · "slider" · "toggle" · "button" · "state" · "animation" · "equation_input" · "code_editor""

• orbit / drag / hover / click — no extra fields.
• animation      — "label", optional "loop": true | false.
• slider         — "label", "range": [min, max, step], "default": <number>.
• toggle         — "label", "options": ["A", "B", ...], "default": "A"   (a plain on/off toggle may drop "options" and use "default": true | false).
• button / state — "label", "states": ["idle", "running", "done"], "default": "idle".
• equation_input — "label", "fields": [ { "id": "...", "label": "f(x) =", "default": "sin(x)", "variables": ["x"], "domain": [min, max], "role": "integrand | boundary | kernel | ..." } ]. "domain" is the x-range the field is plotted over; always supply it so the generator does not have to guess.
• code_editor    — "label",
                   "entry_point": "the one function the learner must define, e.g. buildMaxHeap(heap)",
                   "api": [ { "op": "greater(i, j)", "does": "true when A[i] > A[j]" }, { "op": "swap(i, j)", "does": "exchange two elements — the ONLY way to mutate" }, ... ],
                   "frame": "what one recorded step shows, e.g. 'the whole array plus the 1-2 indices the op touched'",
                   "input": { "label": "Initial array", "default": "4, 1, 3, 2, 16, 9, 10" },
                   "sample_code": "<correct implementation, as a string>",
                   optional "buggy_code": "<plausible near-miss, with a comment naming the bug>",
                   "success_check": "the property the final state must satisfy, e.g. 'every parent >= both of its children'".
  Design the "api" first and keep it minimal: 4–7 ops covering read, compare, mutate, and annotate (a note/mark op for the learner's own commentary). Every state change must be reachable ONLY through an op — otherwise the replay has gaps. The learner writes algorithm logic, never drawing code.

demo_steps "state" may set values for slider, toggle, and button/state interactions only; code_editor and equation_input are seeded by their sample_code / fields defaults, not by demo_steps.

Rules:
- PROJECTION TYPE: pick whichever the source most resembles. Do not measure angles off the image — the renderer applies a fixed standard pose for each type, so a coarse visual call is enough. Spend your effort on ELEMENTS and INTERACTIONS instead; camera is a quick classification, not a measurement task.
  • "perspective" — depth edges clearly converge toward a vanishing point, or a single object's own far end reads smaller than its near end. Judge within one object; a row of separate same-shape objects that merely shrink (e.g. neural-net layers) is not perspective.
  • "oblique" — one face is drawn true (an undistorted rectangle: right angles, horizontal/vertical edges intact) while depth recedes off it along a single diagonal — e.g. stacked feature maps/filter banks drawn as offset same-size copies.
  • "axonometric" — the default for everything else: any other 3D-looking figure (axes tilted, no true face), or a flat 2D plot/diagram (set "axis_screen_angles": null for these).
- CAMERA VIEW: camera_view sets framing only. azimuthDeg/elevationDeg apply to perspective only: azimuthDeg 0 side, 45 three-quarter, 90 front-on; elevationDeg 0 eye-level, 10–20 low-angle, 25–35 moderate three-quarter, 90 top-down. rollDeg is usually 0. heightFraction is how much of the frame the figure should fill (0.5 default, up to 0.75).
- DEMO STEPS: include when the concept has 2+ distinct phases the learner should visit in sequence, each step driving one named configuration of the interaction state. Use [] for a single continuous exploration with no natural sequence.
- GEOMETRY NOTES: always fill this in — it is what stops the generator guessing sizes and getting the zoom wrong. Cover:
  • world-space dimensions, and for oblique/axonometric figures give each box explicitly as X × Y × Z world units, naming which source dimension each axis carries (+X is screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z the receding diagonal).
  • the colour palette, with hex codes where determinable from the source.
  • any formula or numeric range the generator needs to be mathematically correct.
  • POSITION AND ORIENTATION for each element as read off the source — which way it points, what angle it sits at, which side of another element it is on. Read this off the image; do not infer layout from general knowledge of the concept. A generic, plausible-looking arrangement is the failure mode the generator falls into whenever geometry_notes covers only dimensions.
  • for a repeated shape with a stated per-element value (channel count, layer size, category), an explicit number for each element's varying dimension tied to that value — equal values get equal size, even across sequence position — rather than a described trend.
- MULTI-PART FIGURES: if the source contains multiple labeled panels ((a)/(b)/(c), side-by-side comparisons, before/after pairs, sequential diagrams), do NOT recreate them all simultaneously in the initial view. Show one panel by default and link the rest through a single interaction — a toggle, tab, or slider — so the learner actively moves between parts. The transition itself should teach the comparison or progression.
- Prefer interactions that expose relationships in the figure rather than generic controls.

Figure: OChem_11_02_003

AUTHOR-PROVIDED INTERACTION REQUESTS:
Requested interactions:
- Slider for reaction progress: drag from reactants through the bracketed transition state to products, and the geometry morphs from tetrahedral to planar and back while the red electrostatic potential shifts from nucleophile to both ends to leaving group, making charge delocalization during one-step SN2 substitution clear.

Source file:
OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 11: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations

Use these requested interactions when forming the plan. Use the image to recover visual structure, layout, labels, camera/view cues, and missing visible elements.

Planner context:
This figure pairs a three-step reaction scheme with electrostatic potential maps to follow an SN2 substitution, arranged in three stacked rows with the maps on the left and the structures on the right. The top row writes Nu:- in magenta, a plus sign, and a tetrahedral carbon drawn with one bold wedge, one hashed bond, and two plain bonds, joined to a magenta X; alongside it the maps show the free nucleophile as an isolated deep red sphere and the alkyl halide as a two-lobed surface labeled "Tetrahedral" whose halide end is also red. A downward arrow leads to the middle row, where the transition state sits inside square brackets with Nu at the left and X at the right, each carrying a magenta delta- and each tied to the central carbon by a dotted line while the remaining three bonds to that carbon lie in a plane; its map is a wide, symmetric three-lobed surface labeled "Planar", red at both ends and green and yellow across the middle. A second arrow reaches the product row, Nu-C with the wedge and hash now reversed, plus X:-, mapped as a lobed Nu-bearing surface labeled "Tetrahedral" beside a separate red halide sphere. Read down the column, the color scale tracks negative charge leaving the nucleophile, spreading over both ends of the planar species, and settling on the departing halide. The layout supports a single-step mechanism in which backside attack 180 degrees from the leaving group turns the carbon's substituents inside out.

CONTEXT FROM TEXTBOOK:

The top row writes Nu:- in magenta, a plus sign, and a tetrahedral carbon drawn with one bold wedge, one hashed bond, and two plain bonds, joined to a magenta X; alongside it the maps show the free nucleophile as an isolated deep red sphere and the alkyl halide as a two-lobed surface labeled "Tetrahedral" whose halide end is also red. A downward arrow leads to the middle row, where the transition state sits inside square brackets with Nu at the left and X at the right, each carrying a magenta delta- and each tied to the central carbon by a dotted line while the remaining three bonds to that carbon lie in a plane; its map is a wide, symmetric three-lobed surface labeled "Planar", red at both ends and green and yellow across the middle. A second arrow reaches the product row, Nu-C with the wedge and hash now reversed, plus X:-, mapped as a lobed Nu-bearing surface labeled "Tetrahedral" beside a separate red halide sphere. Read down the column, the color scale tracks negative charge leaving the nucleophile, spreading over both ends of the planar species, and settling on the departing halide. The layout supports a single-step mechanism in which backside attack 180 degrees from the leaving group turns the carbon's substituents inside out.

PROJECTION TYPE: perspective
Use the scaffold's true perspective projection after building all geometry. Use this only when the source has real vanishing-point convergence or distance-based size shrinkage; then depth should visibly affect apparent size.

ELEMENTS TO RECREATE IN 3D:
  - Central sp3/sp2 carbon atom (gray sphere) at the origin
  - Three hydrogen atoms (small light-gray spheres) bonded to the central carbon, forming the umbrella that inverts
  - Three C-H bond cylinders
  - Leaving group X (deep red-brown sphere) on the +X side of carbon, connected by a C-X bond cylinder that lengthens and turns dotted at the transition state
  - Nucleophile Nu (deep red-brown sphere) on the -X side of carbon, initially a free isolated sphere, approaching along the backside 180 degrees from X
  - Forming Nu...C partial bond drawn as a dotted/translucent cylinder at the transition state
  - Electrostatic potential surface enveloping the nucleophile alone (isolated red sphere at reactant stage)
  - Two-lobed electrostatic potential surface over the alkyl halide (red at halide lobe, blue/green over the methyl lobe) - labeled 'Tetrahedral'
  - Wide symmetric three-lobed electrostatic potential surface of the transition state, red at both ends, green/yellow across the middle - labeled 'Planar'
  - Two-lobed electrostatic potential surface over the Nu-C product with a separate red halide sphere - labeled 'Tetrahedral'
  - Geometry label text that reads 'Tetrahedral' / 'Planar' / 'Tetrahedral' along the reaction coordinate
  - 2D reaction-scheme panel: 'Nu:-  +  wedge/hash tetrahedral C-X' (top), bracketed transition state with delta- Nu ... C ... X delta- (middle), 'Nu-C with inverted wedge/hash  +  X:-' (bottom)
  - Square brackets around the transition state structure
  - Magenta delta- charge labels on Nu and X in the transition state
  - Downward reaction arrows linking the three scheme rows
  - Color key strip for the electrostatic potential scale (red = most negative through yellow/green to blue = least negative)

GEOMETRY NOTES (world-space scale, color palette, and any formula/value needed for correctness — build to these so sizes, zoom, and colors match the source; do not guess dimensions the notes already specify):
Work in Angstrom-like world units, 1 unit = 1 Å; whole scene spans about ±5 units along X. Reaction axis is the world X axis, screen-right: Nu always on -X, X (leaving group) always on +X, central carbon fixed at the origin. Bond lengths as a function of progress t in [0,1]: C-X = 1.8 + 1.2*t*t*... use C-X = 1.8 at t=0, 2.4 at t=0.5, 4.0 at t=1; C-Nu = 4.0 at t=0, 2.4 at t=0.5, 1.5 at t=1 (symmetric mirror). C-H = 1.09 throughout. The three hydrogens sit on a cone about the X axis: H-C-X angle = 109.5 deg at t=0 (hydrogens tilted toward -X, umbrella opening toward Nu), 90 deg (exactly planar, perpendicular to the axis) at t=0.5, and 70.5 deg at t=1 (tilted toward +X) — this single angle sweep produces the whole inversion. Hydrogens are spaced 120 deg apart in the YZ plane; keep one hydrogen pointing straight down (-Y) so the wedge/hash reversal is visible from the default camera. Sphere radii: carbon 0.45, hydrogen 0.28, halide X and nucleophile Nu 0.62 (drawn as dark red-brown #A0301C in ball-and-stick). Electrostatic potential surface = a smooth blobby isosurface (metaballs / union of scaled spheres, radius ~1.9 around Nu and X, ~1.4 around C, ~1.1 around each H) so at t=0 it reads as one isolated sphere plus a two-lobed peanut, at t=0.5 as a wide symmetric three-lobed dumbbell about 7 units long, at t=1 as a two-lobed peanut plus an isolated sphere. Potential color ramp painted on that surface: most negative red #E8746B / #D9534F, orange #E8945A, yellow #E8E06A, green #8FD18F, blue #7F9FE0 for least negative. Charge weighting: at t=0 the Nu blob is fully red and the halide lobe red while the methyl lobe of the alkyl halide is blue/green; at t=0.5 both end lobes red and the central methyl band green-to-yellow; at t=1 mirror of t=0. Geometry caption text sits centered below the 3D scene: 'Tetrahedral' for t<0.25, 'Planar' near t=0.5, 'Tetrahedral' for t>0.75. The 2D reaction-scheme panel occupies the right third of the frame, three rows stacked top to bottom with downward arrows between them, and the row matching the current slider value is highlighted while the others dim: row 1 'Nu:⁻ + C-X' with Nu, the colon-minus and X in magenta #E0218A and the carbon skeleton in black; row 2 the same skeleton inside black square brackets with magenta dotted bonds out to Nu and X and magenta δ⁻ labels above each; row 3 'Nu-C ... + X:⁻' with wedge and hash swapped relative to row 1. Black text, white background.

DISCRETE CONTROLS (implement every one of these in #ui, each must work independently):

DEMO STEPS (tween through these using goToStep(); each step drives the controls above):
[
  {
    "title": "Reactants",
    "narration": "The nucleophile is a separate, deeply red sphere holding all of the negative charge, while the alkyl halide is a two-lobed tetrahedral surface whose only red region is the halide end.",
    "state": {
      "reactionProgress": 0,
      "surfaceMode": "Both (translucent map)"
    }
  },
  {
    "title": "Backside approach",
    "narration": "Nu moves in along the line directly opposite the C-X bond; the C-X bond stretches and the three hydrogens begin to bend away from the incoming nucleophile.",

      "surfaceMode": "Both (translucent map)"
    }
  },
  {
    "title": "Planar transition state",
    "narration": "At the halfway point the carbon is trigonal planar with Nu and X both half-bonded at 180 degrees. The map is a wide symmetric three-lobed surface, red at both ends and green-yellow across the middle — the charge is delocalized over both Nu and X, each carrying delta-minus.",
    "state": {
      "reactionProgress": 0.5,
      "surfaceMode": "Both (translucent map)"
    }
  },
  {
    "title": "Inversion completes",
    "narration": "Past the transition state the hydrogens snap through to the far side, the new Nu-C bond shortens and the C-X bond breaks — the carbon's configuration has been turned inside out.",
    "state": {
      "reactionProgress": 0.75,
      "surfaceMode": "Ball-and-stick"
    }
  },
  {
    "title": "Products",
    "narration": "The product is again tetrahedral but with the wedge and hash reversed, and the negative charge — the red lobe — now lives entirely on the free leaving group X:-.",
    "state": {
      "reactionProgress": 1,
      "surfaceMode": "Both (translucent map)"
    }
  }
]

CAMERA VIEW (framing only). Call setCameraView({ projection, ...these }) AFTER all geometry is added. Keep the projection MECHANISM from PROJECTION TYPE above (orthographic / sheared-oblique / perspective). For perspective these params set the pose (azimuth/elevation/roll); for the two parallel projections pose is a standard default (see PROJECTION TYPE above), and these params set only roll and framing (heightFraction):
{
  "azimuthDeg": 10,
  "elevationDeg": 12,
  "rollDeg": 0,
  "heightFraction": 0.6
}

NOTES: Build the electrostatic surface as a marching-cubes metaball field (three.js MarchingCubes or a custom implicit mesh) rebuilt each slider frame — resolution ~40³ is enough and keeps the drag responsive; color it per-vertex by evaluating a simple Coulomb-like potential from point charges placed on Nu, C, H and X, with the Nu/X charges linearly interpolated from (-1, 0) at t=0 through (-0.5, -0.5) at t=0.5 to (0, -1) at t=1, then mapped through the red→blue ramp. Render the surface with MeshPhysicalMaterial, transparent, opacity ~0.55, roughness 0.35, slight transmission for the glossy translucent look of the source, and depthWrite false so the ball-and-stick model reads through it. Ball-and-stick uses SphereGeometry plus CylinderGeometry bonds oriented with quaternion lookAt; partial bonds at the transition state are drawn as a row of small spheres (dotted) rather than a solid cylinder, fading the cylinder opacity in/out with bond order. Use two directional lights plus a soft hemisphere light to match the smooth shaded blobs. The 2D scheme panel is best done as an HTML/SVG overlay pinned to the right of the canvas rather than in-scene geometry, with CSS opacity for the active-row highlight. Labels 'Tetrahedral'/'Planar' as a CSS2DObject or plain HTML caption under the canvas. The play animation simply sweeps reactionProgress 0→1→0 with an ease-in-out and writes back to the slider so the two controls stay in sync.

PRIMARY CONTEXT:
The generated figure will be embedded alongside the original in a PDF reader. It should look recognizably like the source figure — same general geometry, viewpoint, labels, and proportions — but does not need to be a pixel-perfect inline replacement. Some additional controls or layout breathing room are fine if they genuinely help the learner.

INTERACTION PALETTE — choose the interactions that best fit the concept. Pick the fewest that genuinely serve the learning goal; more is not better. In "teaches", say what the learner understands, not what the control does.

• orbit / drag — rotate/move the scene. When depth or 3D shape IS the concept.
• hover — reveal a label on demand. When showing every label at once clutters.
• click — highlight one element. When focus on one part of a busy scene matters.
• slider — sweep one continuous variable. When dragging it visibly transforms the figure.
• toggle — switch between 2+ named views. For before/after or dual views (e.g. spatial ↔ frequency).
• button / state — step through discrete phases. When distinct stages should be visited deliberately.
• animation — self-playing motion. When the concept is inherently dynamic and a slider can't convey it.
• equation_input — learner types math, parsed at runtime. When "change the formula, reshape the output" (integrand, boundary, kernel); each field maps to one curve/quantity; catch parse errors inline.
• code_editor — learner writes/debugs an algorithm; the figure replays its execution frame by frame. Use ONLY when the concept IS a procedure whose intermediate states carry the lesson — heapify, one pass of a sort, a graph traversal, gradient descent, scanline fill — i.e. the question a learner has is "in what order does it touch the data, and why". Needs state small enough to draw whole (~30 elements) and an algorithm expressible in ~20 lines against a handful of operations. Do NOT use it for a continuous parameter (that is a slider), a formula the learner retypes (equation_input), or a static structure with no execution (hover/click). • animation      — "label", optional "loop": true | false.
• slider         — "label", "range": [min, max, step], "default": <number>.
• toggle         — "label", "options": ["A", "B", ...], "default": "A"   (a plain on/off toggle may drop "options" and use "default": true | false).

  • "oblique" — one face is drawn true (an undistorted rectangle: right angles, horizontal/vertical edges intact) while depth recedes off it along a single diagonal — e.g. stacked feature maps/filter banks drawn as offset same-size copies.
  • "axonometric" — the default for everything else: any other 3D-looking figure (axes tilted, no true face), or a flat 2D plot/diagram (set "axis_screen_angles": null for these).
- CAMERA VIEW: camera_view sets framing only. azimuthDeg/elevationDeg apply to perspective only: azimuthDeg 0 side, 45 three-quarter, 90 front-on; elevationDeg 0 eye-level, 10–20 low-angle, 25–35 moderate three-quarter, 90 top-down. rollDeg is usually 0. heightFraction is how much of the frame the figure should fill (0.5 default, up to 0.75).
